items.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was very proud of the fact that sometimes Louis Jordan would come by and rehearse with the band.

ctx.x: It’s the fraternal organization connected to the Elks period. These were the independent high B.P.O. And Pop used to… he was a tremendous mechanic, he was a great mechanic, and to give you a history of my father, when we were very young, it was just my sister, myself and Jimmy was just born when we were living in West Philadelphia, we had first moved from the South, Jimmy was born in Philadelphia. But Lizzy and I were brought up from Wilmington. And at that time, my father had a business as a mechanic. He had his…

We were really well off until the NRA, the National Recovery Act, during the Depression came, and it drove my father out of business. The little guy got squeezed out somehow under that recovery act. And it was a couple of years when my father had to be on WPA with Works Project [Progress] Administration, and he’d go stand around with a shovel to get a handout, more or less, and we were like welfare recipients.
